_fixture.note: Derived, not recorded. The recorded captures predate `fps`, `tbr`, `vcodec` and `acodec` on a format (SEC-002: a fixture carries only what the projection reads, and the projection did not read them until T-107). REQ-003 names all four as columns, so the format table's tests need a fixture that has them. This is that fixture, and it is NOT evidence for Phase 3's exit criterion 1 — matching `yt-dlp -F` needs a recorded capture, which T-185 owns.

_fixture.why_this_source: The same public-domain item the recorded capture uses, so the shape is real; only the fields the recorded capture could not carry are synthetic. formats[3] and formats[4] are an explicitly audio-only and an explicitly video-only stream - `vcodec: none` and `acodec: none`, yt-dlp's own spelling - which is the pair REQ-008 merges and which NO acceptable recorded source supplies: media.ccc.de reports `vcodec: none` beside a named acodec, but its API states no licence for any event, so ai/TESTING.md 5's freely-licensed rule rules it out. T-188 owns that search; OPS-013 is what permits the gap while it is owned and declared. formats[5] carries neither fps nor bitrate nor size, so the table's placeholder path has a row too. formats[6] names a vcodec and no acodec at all - media.ccc.de's real shape for a video recording - which is UNKNOWN rather than video-only, because the file certainly has sound and nothing said so. It is here because a mutation reading that as video-only survived every other fixture. formats[7] is an HLS audio rendition - `vcodec: none` with no acodec at all, which is what a real EXT-X-MEDIA:TYPE=AUDIO group produces - and formats[8] denies both streams, as a storyboard does. The first is the audio half; the second is neither half. Both boundaries were found by driving a real local HLS presentation through yt-dlp for T108-R1.
